text:
alex: Quick heads up — after merging kernel-selection v2 (PR #472) I see continuous-batcher tail latency increase on dedicated pools. Not huge but p95 for short sequences jumped from ~60ms to ~220ms. Spikes visible in token/sec and queue_depth panels. Anyone else seeing this?

deploy-bot: deploy started by alex — canary rollout to dedicated-1 at 2026-03-10T14:22Z

sasha: I saw the same. Did a sampling profile — kernel fallback path is firing when KV-cache miss rate climbs above ~12%. That triggers an extra memcpy + unoptimized kernel path for quantized models.

ryan: can you paste the prom queries you used for batch/util and queue metrics?

sasha: sure, quick ones I used: 
```promql
sum(rate(batcher_batch_tokens_total[1m])) by (pool) / sum(rate(batcher_capacity_tokens[1m])) by (pool)
```
and queue depth: 
```promql
sum(batcher_queue_depth) by (pool)
```
Added kv cache hits as: `sum(rate(kv_cache_hits_total[1m])) / sum(rate(kv_cache_requests_total[1m]))`.

maya: I overlaid kv_cache_hit_ratio vs batch_size in grafana — the hit ratio dip lines up with queue_push_latency jumps. Dashboard link: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/abc123/batcher-overview?view=tokenmeter

alex: kernel-selection logs also show the selector switching to `generic_kernel` for 4–8 token sequences. Looks like the quantized optimized kernel is rejected when a compatibility flag isn't set, so we compile/fallback at runtime.

sasha: my hypothesis — our token_budget target of 128 is too aggressive for short-request workloads. With small budgets we form smaller micro-batches and more often hit cold KV states, causing kernel churn.

ryan: can we try a token_budget=64 for short-seq-heavy pools and see? Maybe also increase KV prefetch window to smooth misses.

maya: I ran a 30m canary on dedicated-1 with token_budget=64. p95 improved to ~80ms and batch_util went from ~32% to ~58%. kv_cache_hit_ratio increased by ~4 percentage points.

alex: nice. I also grabbed a CPU flame from perf: heavy spend in `copy_and_pad` (~14%) and `kernel_dispatch` (~22%). That matches extra memcpy and dispatch work when fallback happens.

sasha: opened runtime PR to avoid the memcpy on fallback (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/501 — adds an in-place pad path and guard to skip realloc when compatibility check fails.

deploy-bot: canary health OK, no increase in 5xx or infra errors.

ryan: action items:
- sasha: finish the memcpy-avoid patch and add a unit that asserts no extra memmove on fallback
- maya: run a 24h canary with token_budget=64 and collect tokenmeter + kv panels
- alex: add an alert: `batch_util < 20%` for >5m AND `kv_hit_ratio < 10%` to trigger an ops paging runbook

sasha: I'll also add a grafana panel that overlays `kernel_switch_rate` with `kv_cache_miss` so we can validate coupling over time.

maya: FYI this skew was only reproducible on quantized gpt-small variants; fp16 gpt-large didn't show the same behavior.

alex: thanks all — let's regroup after the 24h canary. :thumbsup:
